answer: Physical presence is the scarce resource: each identity commits one responder to a cell for 30 days. Verifiers in three regions send simultaneous nonces timed from a common anchor; replies must come from that cell and each forms a pearl, a signed round-trip sample anyone can check against light-time bounds. One host yields one vector; relaying adds delay, so clones cannot satisfy many cells. An honest agent uses its own host; 1,000 fakes need 1,000 responders for 30 days. A sable mark and loss follow only when samples jointly prove a faster-than-light reply or two distant vectors at once.
